assumptions: fired duty = temperature-feasible import after FEHE and tail-gas firing
H3-a.uncertainty: Python fired duty is 13.8-15.2 kW below Aspen at the same T and X for all five catalysts (spread 1.4 kW, so the T-dependence is reproduced within 1.4 kW over 95 K); FEHE duty offset +20.8 kW (model form, task X1).
H3-a.envelope: 20 bar, X 0.95 (equal conversion), 499-594 degC, with and without FEHE. With FEHE the saving is about 0.26 kW per K (25 kW from 594 to 499 degC, about 5 % of fired duty); it exceeds the absolute Python-Aspen offset (15 kW) only for a temperature drop of about 60 K or more (Ru/Al2O3, Ru/MgO against Ni; not the NiRu/CeO2 catalysts, 4-5 kW). Without FEHE 31-163 kW. The direction is kinetics-independent; WHICH catalyst reaches which T rests on extrapolated laws.
H3-a.reason: Computed (Python, cross-checked against Aspen at the same T and X); the reduction at equal conversion is not a built-in assumption. CORRECTION to Phase 1: the Aspen fixed-inventory runs reach unequal conversion (Ni 0.9589 against Ru/Al2O3 0.9496); most of the 102 kW (17 %) Aspen difference comes from that conversion difference (less unconverted NH3 burnt in the tail gas), not from temperature. At equal conversion the saving is 25 kW with FEHE. When each design is cost-optimised at derived central prices the Ru-containing designs move to HIGHER temperatures than Ni and the saving disappears or reverses (H3-c): the energy claim holds for low-T operating points, not for cost-optimal designs.

H3-b.uncertainty: no law validated at 20 bar; Ni/MgO and Ru/MgO laws fail their literature comparison at 1 atm (KIN-NI-PRED, KIN-RU-PRED)
H3-b.envelope: 20 bar, X 0.95, 100 kg per 100 kmol/h NH3; equilibrium limits X 0.95 to about 485 degC and above
H3-b.reason: The temperature ordering at fixed inventory (Ru/Al2O3 499 < Ru/MgO 522 < NiRu 572-576 < Ni/MgO 594 degC) rests on laws extrapolated to 20 bar, and the Ni reference law is in class 'extrapolated'. Among laws validated against literature only (Ru/Al2O3, NiRu/CeO2; pressure-extrapolated) the Ru/Al2O3 law reaches the target about 73-77 K lower than the NiRu laws, but no validated Ni law exists to compare with. This task adds no kinetic evidence.

assumptions: catalyst prices DERIVED from metal content + 32.2 USD/kg non-metal part (no quotation exists)
FEHE U central 72.5 W/(m2 K) (derived), varied 35-150
reactor CAPEX by NH3 feed (frozen basis) or by catalyst mass (sensitivity)
no Ru recovery credit (no sourced refining charge or recovery fraction)
H3-c.uncertainty: Ru price (USGS 2025 average to Nov 2026 JM spot), lifetime 1-5 yr, NH3 300-1000 USD/t, fuel price, natural-gas heat, electricity 0.084-0.222 USD/kWh, discount 0.085-0.10, 7000-8000 h, U 35-150, reactor cost driver, rates /5. The FEHE cost is a step function of temperature (4 -> 5 shells in series between 537 and 538 degC at U central, +0.235 MUSD TCI, about +0.023 USD/kg): in the 'exchanger' mode it pins several optima at 537 degC and is of the same size as the catalyst differences; the 'reference' mode (no exchanger response) is reported beside it.
H3-c.envelope: 20 bar, X 0.95, PSA 0.85, grey 450 USD/t base; Python flowsheet (cost-optimal) or Aspen duties (fixed 100 kg)

threshold.breakeven_price: catalyst_breakeven.csv (fixed and re-optimised); compared with the metal-content floor and the central price

H3-c.reason: (1) Kinetic operating temperatures at equal conversion 0.95 (90-100 kg, Python flowsheet, FEHE costed): break-even prices Ru/Al2O3 1506, Ru/MgO 1297, 5Ni1Ru/CeO2 177, 2.5Ni0.5Ru/CeO2 151 USD/kg against floors 1775, 1109, 223, 111 and central 4791, 3006, 628, 330; break-even below the metal floor for ['Ru/Al2O3', '5Ni1Ru/CeO2'], above the central price for none. (2) Cost-optimal designs (both re-optimised, exchanger mode): low-T catalyst cheaper beyond the resolution 0.0060 USD/kg for none; Ru-containing designs at a LOWER temperature than Ni for none: at derived prices the economic optimum of an expensive catalyst is a small charge at high temperature, so the energy saving that the claim rests on is not chosen. (3) Against Ni at sourced design temperatures (Cho 735.52, Mehr 760 degC), the kinetics-free Ni threshold temperatures are {'Ru/Al2O3': 670.2141573981465, 'Ru/MgO': 675.556909342881, '5Ni1Ru/CeO2': 639.7505259335887, '2.5Ni0.5Ru/CeO2': 539.6198716644107}; the low-T designs win against those Ni designs but lose against the AmCraX Ni/MgO optimum (537 degC, extrapolated law). The Ni design temperature therefore decides the ranking, sourced values and the extrapolated model straddle the threshold, and every LCOH difference is below 1 % of LCOH. Resolved low-T wins in 1 of 100 sensitivity rows.

assumptions: Cho operating points rebuilt on AmCraX boundaries (no compression, recycle, TSA, expander)
supplementary fuel needed when the temperature-feasible process heat import after tail-gas firing is > 0
H3-e.uncertainty: PSA recovery 0.70-0.95; boundary differences to Cho; Python only at Cho's points
H3-e.envelope: X 0.97; Ni 735.52 degC / 24.34 bar; Ru 566.69 degC / 10 bar
H3-e.reason: The fuel need at fixed T, P and X is kinetics-independent. Whether Ru needs no supplementary fuel while Ni does depends on PSA recovery: Cho's pattern appears only for recoveries between the two thresholds. At Cho's own 0.756 neither design needs process heat import on AmCraX boundaries; at the AmCraX 0.85 both do. The source value 0.756 lies outside the window, so on AmCraX boundaries the claim is not reproduced; because the boundaries differ (Cho's extra units), this is a reproduction finding, not a contradiction of Cho's own flowsheet. Secondary row.

H3-f.reason: The sign of the REC difference changes with the inventory basis at Cho's prices; at derived prices of a 3 wt% Ru catalyst the Ru REC advantage shrinks or reverses. Cho's 7 % is not reproduced; the AmCraX CAPEX does not respond to T and P as Cho's does. Secondary row.
